records.confirmation_evidence: MIT Student Financial Services' own page 'Apply for aid: International students' (https://sfs.mit.edu/undergraduate-students/apply-for-aid/international) states: 'International students are considered for aid using the same process that we use for all applicants. We are committed to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need for international students, just as we are for domestic students.' Its deadlines page states 'Early Action November 30', 'Regular Action February 15', 'Transfer February 15' and that 'Application deadlines are the same for both domestic and international students.' Its MIT Scholarship page states 'The median MIT Scholarship was $73,666 for 2025-2026' and 'About 58% of our undergraduates receive MIT Scholarships.'

programme_detail_official.study_mode: Full-time undergraduate enrolment in the College
programme_detail_official.application_method: Complete the International Student Financial Aid Worksheet electronically in the applicant's UChicago Account during the admissions process
programme_detail_official.application_route: Apply for admission and financial aid at the same time; the CSS Profile and FAFSA are not used for international applicants
requirements: Complete the International Student Financial Aid Worksheet in the UChicago Account
Do not submit the CSS Profile or the FAFSA
Do not submit the Certification of Finances form with the aid application
Re-apply for need-based aid in subsequent years if aid was received in the first year
documents: 2025 tax forms or the home country equivalent, translated into English and converted to US dollars
Employer income statement or bank statements showing recurring salary deposits where no tax filing is required
Asset Verification Form with statements of checking, savings, investment and non-primary property values
programme_detail_official.english_requirement_note: The financial aid pages state no English-language test requirement; they require that non-US tax documents be translated into English and converted into US dollars.
selection_criteria: For merit scholarships, outstanding academic achievement, demonstrated leadership and commitment to the community
award_holder_conditions: International students who receive need-based aid in the first year re-apply for need-based aid in future years
Students who do not apply for aid during the admissions process cannot apply later
Stipend recipients who want direct deposit must open a US bank account
supplements_or_initiatives: Merit scholarships for international applicants, notified on a rolling basis through the end of April

official_contacts.general: University of Chicago Office of Financial Aid, 1101 E. 58th Street, Walker 101, Chicago, IL 60637; College Admissions, Rosenwald Hall 105, 1101 E. 58th Street, Chicago, IL 60637

programme_detail_official.description: The University of Chicago meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted international undergraduate applicants who applied for funding during the admissions process, through loan-free grant aid and an international student stipend. International aid applicants complete an International Student Financial Aid Worksheet rather than the CSS Profile or FAFSA. International transfer applicants are not eligible.
programme_detail_official.program_type: Undergraduate need-based institutional financial aid and merit scholarship programme
programme_detail_official.coverage: Full demonstrated need as loan-free grants, plus an international student stipend for billed and other costs

application_readiness_checklist: Apply to the University of Chicago College and request financial aid in the same admissions round
Open the UChicago Account and complete the International Student Financial Aid Worksheet
Collect 2025 tax forms or the home-country equivalent, plus employer or bank evidence where no tax filing exists
Complete the Asset Verification Form with statements of checking, savings, investment and non-primary property values
Arrange English translation and US dollar conversion of all non-US documents
common_rejection_risks: Waiting until after the admissions decision to request aid, which the University rules out
Submitting the CSS Profile or the FAFSA as an international applicant, which the University says not to do
Applying as an international transfer applicant, who are excluded from need-based aid and merit scholarships
Missing the November 15, January 15 or February 15 institutional aid deadline for the chosen round
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any living costs above the stipend, since the University notes 'Expenses beyond tuition and fees (including food and housing, travel to and from Chicago, etc.) will need to be paid out of pocket or with the help of the international stipend'
Summer term costs, which the University excludes from its funding guarantees
document_audit: Completed International Student Financial Aid Worksheet in the UChicago Account
Translated and dollar-converted 2025 tax forms or employer and bank income evidence
Completed Asset Verification Form with account statements
Confirmation that the CSS Profile and FAFSA were not submitted for the aid application

alerts.message: International students are eligible for financial aid only if they apply for funding during the admissions process and cannot apply later, so decide before submitting the admission application.
The international student stipend is paid directly to the student, either by direct deposit to a US bank account or by mailed paper check, so plan to open a US bank account after enrolment.
If an institutional aid deadline falls on a weekend or holiday the University moves it to the next business day.

submission_workflow: Create a UChicago Account and submit the admission application in the chosen round
Complete the International Student Financial Aid Worksheet electronically in that account
Upload proof of family income and assets with translations and dollar conversions
Watch for the admissions decision and the aid offer, and re-apply for need-based aid in later years

institution_check_required: The current cost of attendance figure for 2026-2027, which the Office of Financial Aid publishes on a separate costs page and which varies by on-campus, commuter and off-campus status
Whether an English-language proficiency requirement applies for admission, which the financial aid pages do not address
